newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Seoul shrs seen falling, foreigners may retreat.
newsitem.headline: Seoul shrs seen falling, foreigners may retreat.

text.p: Seoul stocks are expected to consolidate on Tuesday as investors, especially foreigners, turn cautious after Monday's volatile trading, brokers said.
"Foreign buying has been a main impetus to the recent rally. But foreign investors are likely to take a break," Na Min-ho, a broker at Daishin Securities.

The composite stock index closed 1.62 points higher at 758.39 on Monday. Trading volume rose to 84.89 million shares, the second highest level since the market's opening. The largest volume was 85.17 million recorded in July, 1995, brokers said.
Brokers said Monday's clashes between militant students and riot police would have little impact on the market.
"Investors are more concerned about economic factors," said a Hyundai Securities broker.
A riot policeman died on Monday in the clashes, the first fatality in four days of violent protest in Seoul to demand the resignation of President Kim Young-sam.
Brokers said financial shares would react to an expected report on financial reforms to President today.
The reforms would include changes in bank ownership.
Construction shares are likely to fall, affected by the troubled Hanshin Construction, brokers said.
On Monday, Hanshin formally defaulted on debts as it failed to honour 2.6 billion won worth of debts, major creditor SEOULBANK said.
A SEOULBANK official said the nation's 24th largest construction company first defaulted on 21.8 billion won in debt obligations on Saturday.
Hanshin sought court receivership from its creditors on last Friday after determining it would be unable to pay its debts.
